_names: Terminologia Anatomica individual terms (explicitly public domain)
_definitions: Gray's Anatomy 1918, original scan (PD-US). Reused verbatim from the region label files already in this repo.
_geometry: Auto pins from TotalSegmentator `total` (Apache-2.0 code and weights) on the FULL Visible Human frozenCT stack: slices 1006-2882, 1877 contiguous 1 mm slices, vertex to feet, verified gap-free. Run on a 62 GB VM; this volume is ~984 MB and cannot be segmented on the 8 GB laptop at all.
_why_skeleton_only: The whole-body run is deliberately restricted to the SKELETON. Every non-bone class this cadaver offers has already been measured and rejected elsewhere in this atlas: lung reads -540 to -570 HU against -700 to -850 in a living aerated lung so no lobe is resolvable; liver, spleen and kidney share one 25-90 HU band without contrast and cannot be separated; and every pelvic muscle mask read median -13 to -21 HU with 32-40% of its voxels below -30 HU, i.e. fat rather than the +20 to +70 HU muscle must read. Bone is the one tissue whose contrast on this series is unambiguous, and the HU check is re-run per structure before any of these pins ship.
_why_no_sides: No side is asserted anywhere in this atlas. All 24 rib classes collapse to `rib`, and left/right humerus, scapula, clavicle, femur and hip collapse to one structure each. On this cadaver two independent landmarks disagree about left and right on an 8% margin that flips sign, and TotalSegmentator's own side assignment was measured wrong on the pelvis (gluteus minimus 848 voxels one side against 36293 the other). Collapsing removes the error rather than shipping it; one pin per connected component still shows the reviewer both sides.
_why_no_levels: Individual ribs and vertebrae are NOT numbered. All 26 vertebral classes collapse into the three REGIONS - cervical, thoracic, lumbar - plus the sacrum. A region is honestly determinable from position in a head-to-feet stack; a level is not, and this atlas does not claim one.

skull.name: Skull
skull.definition: The skull is the skeleton of the head, comprising the cranium, which encloses the brain, and the mandible. Its bones are united by sutures except at the temporomandibular joint.

cervical-vertebra.name: Cervical vertebra
cervical-vertebra.definition: The cervical vertebrae are the smallest of the movable vertebrae and bear foramina in their transverse processes.

thoracic-vertebra.name: Thoracic vertebra
thoracic-vertebra.definition: The thoracic vertebrae are distinguished by costal facets on the sides of their bodies.

lumbar-vertebra.name: Lumbar vertebra
lumbar-vertebra.definition: The lumbar vertebrae are the largest segments of the movable part of the vertebral column.

sacrum.name: Sacrum
sacrum.definition: The sacrum is a large triangular bone formed by the union of five vertebrae, wedged between the two hip bones.

rib.name: Rib
rib.definition: The ribs are elastic arches of bone forming the greater part of the thoracic skeleton.

sternum.name: Sternum
sternum.definition: The sternum is a flat narrow bone forming the middle of the anterior thoracic wall.

clavicle.name: Clavicle
clavicle.definition: The clavicle forms the anterior portion of the shoulder girdle.

hip-bone.name: Hip bone
hip-bone.definition: The hip bone is a large flattened irregular bone formed by the ilium, ischium and pubis.

_why_caps: A whole-body cut shows an enormous number of repeats - a coronal view crosses every rib and the entire vertebral column. Identical repeated labels saturate both gutters and teach nothing after the first few.
_why_costal_cartilage_dropped: REJECTED on measurement: only 1.3% of the costal-cartilage mask reads above 200 HU. This cadaver was 38 years old and its costal cartilage is not calcified, so the mask sits on soft tissue rather than bone. Position was right (slices 377-531) but there is no bone there to point at.
_why_limb_bones_dropped: REJECTED because the cadaver's ARMS lie alongside the trunk all the way down to the thighs, and TotalSegmentator labels those long bones as femur / humerus / scapula. Measured, not suspected: at chest level (z 390-500) the voxels called `femur` sit at relx +0.82 to +0.97, i.e. hard against the body edge where the arm is, not inside the trunk; `scapula` does the same at pelvis level (z 760) and `humerus` at thigh level (z 1210). Their z-mass spans give it away too - scapula 649 slices, humerus 1007, femur 855, against 68 for the clavicle. The same trap is documented in segment_thorax_ct.py ('a humerus becomes a rib'). Femur and hip bone ARE delivered correctly by the dedicated ct-pelvis-* modules, whose crop excludes the arms. Fixing this in the whole body needs an arm-exclusion mask, which is future work, not a claim to ship now.
_verification: Every surviving structure passed two checks. (1) HU: percentage of mask voxels above 200 HU - skull 76.1, cervical vertebra 92.2, thoracic 70.9, lumbar 72.9, sacrum 59.9, rib 76.3, sternum 46.8, clavicle 56.3, hip bone 63.8. (2) Position: the p1-p99 z-mass of each structure falls in correct head-to-feet anatomical ORDER - skull 11-219, cervical 161-275, clavicle 265-333, thoracic 264-548, sternum 361-504, rib 306-606, lumbar 506-757, sacrum 752-855, hip bone 733-922, on a stack where slice 0 is the vertex and 1876 is the feet. That ordering was not imposed; it fell out of the data, and it is the strongest single check that the whole-body geometry is sound.
